dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real normed vector space E, fields q and production, and flux:E→E, requires spatial interval integrability of q at every time, temporal interval integrability of flux(q(x,·)) at every position, spatial interval integrability of production at every time, temporal interval integrability of every spatial production integral, and the balance identity on every choice of spatial and temporal endpoints.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The sole hypothesis supplies all four integrability conditions and the identity Q_ab(t)−Q_ab(s)=∫_s^t [speed·q(a,τ)−speed·q(b,τ)]dτ+∫_s^t∫_a^b production(x,τ)dx dτ. The first conclusion repeats this entire hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: Requires spatial interval integrability of q at every time, temporal interval integrability of flux(q(x,·)) at every position, and the source-free balance identity Q_ab(t)−Q_ab(s)=∫_s^t [flux(q(a,τ))−flux(q(b,τ))]dτ for every a,b,s,t.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With flux(v)=speed·v, this entire predicate is equivalent to vanishing of all iterated production integrals; its negation is equivalent to existence of one nonzero iterated production integral.

binders: Let V be the fixed real normed vector space Fin 1→Real, consisting of functions on the singleton index set {0}, canonically identifiable with the real numbers.
For every pair of fields q, production:Real→Real→V, with first argument x interpreted as position and second argument t interpreted as time.
For every speed c∈Real, fixed throughout the proposition, define flux(v)=c·v.
The identities and the universal zero-integral condition quantify independently over every a,b,s,t∈Real.
The nonzero-integral condition existentially quantifies a,b,s,t in that order for the fixed q, production, and c. These witnesses need not be uniform across choices of the fields or speed.

The derivative conclusion first fixes arbitrary a,b∈Real and then quantifies over almost every t∈Real. Its bound variable s is the argument of the function being differentiated, independently of other occurrences of s.
hypotheses: For every a,b,t∈Real, x↦q(x,t) is Lebesgue interval integrable from a to b.
For every x,s,t∈Real, τ↦c·q(x,τ) is Lebesgue interval integrable from s to t.
For every a,b,t∈Real, x↦production(x,t) is Lebesgue interval integrable from a to b.
For every a,b,s,t∈Real, τ↦∫_a^b production(x,τ)dx is Lebesgue interval integrable from s to t.
For every a,b,s,t∈Real, Q_ab(t)−Q_ab(s)=∫_s^t B_ab(τ)dτ+P_ab(s,t), where Q_ab, B_ab, and P_ab are defined below.
conclusions: LocalDef001(q,flux,production) holds, repeating all five conditions in the hypothesis.
LocalDef002(q,flux) holds if and only if P_ab(s,t)=0_V for every a,b,s,t∈Real.
LocalDef002(q,flux) fails if and only if there exist a,b,s,t∈Real such that P_ab(s,t)≠0_V.
For every a,b∈Real, for Lebesgue-almost every t∈Real, the function s↦Q_ab(s) has derivative B_ab(t)+R_ab(t) at t.
mathematical_definitions: All vector operations are pointwise on the sole index 0; in particular (c·v)(0)=c v(0), and 0_V is the function with sole coordinate zero.
For any vector-valued f, ∫_a^b f(x)dx denotes its oriented Bochner interval integral: the Lebesgue integral over (a,b] minus the Lebesgue integral over (b,a].
Q_ab(t)=∫_a^b q(x,t)dx is the spatially integrated q field at time t.
R_ab(t)=∫_a^b production(x,t)dx is the spatially integrated production field at time t.
B_ab(t)=c·q(a,t)−c·q(b,t) is the left-endpoint flux minus the right-endpoint flux.
P_ab(s,t)=∫_s^t R_ab(τ)dτ=∫_s^t (∫_a^b production(x,τ)dx)dτ, with the spatial integral performed first.
LocalDef002(q,flux) means that every spatial slice of q is interval integrable, every temporal slice of flux(q) is interval integrable, and Q_ab(t)−Q_ab(s)=∫_s^t B_ab(τ)dτ for every a,b,s,t.

Having derivative d∈V at t means the ordinary real-parameter derivative exists with value d; equivalently, the sole coordinate's difference quotient tends to d(0) as its nonzero real increment tends to zero.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For arbitrary one-component real fields q and production on all real positions and times, and any fixed real speed c, suppose the spatial slices of both fields, the temporal slices of c·q, and the temporal functions obtained by spatially integrating production are integrable on every bounded interval, and suppose the integrated balance identity holds for all spatial and temporal endpoints. Then all these conditions continue to hold, and the iterated production integral equals the change in spatially integrated q minus the time-integrated left-minus-right flux. The source-free integrated balance predicate is equivalent to all such production integrals being zero; its failure is equivalent to one such integral being nonzero. Finally, for each fixed pair of spatial endpoints, the spatial integral of q is differentiable at almost every time, with derivative equal to c·q at the left endpoint minus c·q at the right endpoint plus the spatial integral of production.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The state space is fixed at one real component. The generic space parameters in LocalDef001 and LocalDef002 do not make this target a theorem for arbitrary dimensions or arbitrary normed spaces.
Position and time range over all real numbers. There is no nonnegative-time restriction, bounded physical domain, initial condition, or boundary condition.

There are no ordering assumptions on a,b or s,t. All integrals are oriented. If a=b or s=t, the corresponding iterated production integral is zero, so a nonzero witness necessarily has distinct spatial endpoints and distinct temporal endpoints.

The speed is a constant real scalar, with no positivity or nonzero assumption. When c=0, temporal integrability of c·q is automatic and does not itself impose temporal integrability on q at fixed positions.

The theorem is conditional on the full integrated balance identity and four families of integrability assumptions. It does not construct fields satisfying them or derive the balance identity from a separate differential equation. The first conclusion simply repeats the assumption.
The assumptions are consistent, for example when q and production are identically zero, so there is no forced logical vacuity.

The derivative statement has quantifier order 'for every a,b, almost every t'; the exceptional null set may depend on a and b. It does not assert one common full-measure set of times valid simultaneously for all real endpoint pairs.
The derivative is that of the spatial integral of q. The proposition does not assert pointwise differentiability of q in space or time, or the pointwise equation ∂_t q+c∂_x q=production.
The equivalences concern vanishing of all iterated production integrals, not an explicitly stated pointwise or almost-everywhere vanishing condition on production.
No positivity, physical units, entropy condition, uniqueness, or existence of solutions is encoded by the names q, production, and speed.

The hypothesis explicitly controls slices and iterated integrals. It does not explicitly require joint measurability or joint integrability on space-time rectangles, nor state an interchange of integration order.

Bochner integrals are totalized in Lean, but the hypothesis supplies interval integrability for the integrals appearing here; the flux-difference integrals are integrable by subtraction of the two assumed integrable flux slices.
